resources.string: Apollo and driving assistance
Apollo on a compatible FREE 318 · setup stays in the factory controls.
Set up in the vehicle
Open Vehicle → Driving assistance. On a compatible vehicle, enable TLC before NOA.
If a control is unavailable in Guest, check what the factory page asks for. Follow its prompts for vehicle account, training or service access.
Check this head unit
Read the head-unit software details and cached factory requests. Check access and assistance status in the vehicle.
FREE 318 owner manual
Answer for the factory page
While a switch is on, Controls answers inside the factory settings app. Turning it off takes the answer away again. None of this confirms what the vehicle did.
Show Apollo controls in Guest

The factory settings page asks its own subscription provider whether Apollo is subscribed. Controls answers that question with the stock subscribed answer, so the page can offer the Apollo controls while the profile stays Guest. The answer is held in memory only: it is gone when the switch is off or the factory app restarts, and nothing is written to the vehicle.
Send the assistance state to the controller (experimental)

With the car in Park and stopped, the factory software is asked once to send its assistance bundle to the driving-assistance controller. Changing another switch does not send it again. One send covers eighteen named fields at once, the head unit cannot read the original values back, and there is no verified way back. An accepted request does not confirm the controller state. Use it at your own risk.
Use the Baidu equipment branch (experimental)

The factory page is told to select the Baidu equipment branch and the domestic region. Only what the page shows changes; the vehicle configuration readings behind it stay as they are. On a vehicle with another supplier the page can offer controls the vehicle does not have. Use it at your own risk.

Stop the car in Park before sending the assistance state to the controller.

Controls starts the factory settings worker with the first switch and stops it with the last one. The change reaches the factory page within a second. Read Apollo diagnostics still reports cached requests only, never a controller state.
